title: Relative universal cones as initial or final objects of an exponential corner
statement:
Use [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the joins and mapping-space definition of relative universal diagrams in [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and the relative-initial and relative-final predicates in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary]. Let $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an isofibration of quasicategories (an inner fibration lifting equivalence edges with a specified source), and let $K$ be any small simplicial set. For $\epsilon\in\{\triangleright,\triangleleft\}$ set $X_\epsilon=\operatorname{Fun}(K^\epsilon,\mathcal C)$ and
$$p_\epsilon:X_\epsilon\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D)}\operatorname{Fun}(K^\epsilon,\mathcal D),\qquad u\longmapsto(u|_K,pu).$$
These are isofibrations between quasicategories. A diagram $u:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$ is a $p$-colimit diagram if and only if its vertex in $X_{\triangleright}$ is $p_{\triangleright}$-initial. A diagram $u:K^{\triangleleft}\to\mathcal C$ is a $p$-limit diagram if and only if its vertex in $X_{\triangleleft}$ is $p_{\triangleleft}$-final. No colimits or limits other than the specified diagrams are assumed.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.13 and its colimit dual, interpreted using Proposition 7.1.6.19 (02X1), condition (2). The isofibration clause is Proposition 4.4.5.1 (01F1). Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; online source, archive wanted.

proof.text: Fix either sign and write $L=K^\epsilon$, $X=\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal C)$, $A=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$, $V=\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal D)$, $W=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D)$ and $T=A\times_W V$. The pure-factor inclusion $K\hookrightarrow L$ in the degreewise join is injective in every degree: it is the summand whose other factor has degree $-1$. Apply the exponential-corner assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] to this inclusion and $p$. It gives quasicategories $X,T$ and the claimed isofibration $q=p_\epsilon:X\to T$. The same assertion applied to the restriction with target $\mathcal D$ gives quasicategories $V,W$ and an isofibration $s:V\to W$; $A$ is also a quasicategory by its restriction assertion with target $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.5.1 and Corollary 4.4.5.3; application to the pure-factor inclusion in the join.

proof.text: For any $a,b\in T$, write their coordinates as $(a_A,a_V)$ and $(b_A,b_V)$ and their common images in $W$ as $a_W,b_W$. Using the arrow mapping spaces $U$ defined in [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], the degreewise pullback definition gives the simplicial identity $$U_T(a,b)=U_A(a_A,b_A)\times_{U_W(a_W,b_W)}U_V(a_V,b_V).$$ Indeed a simplex on the left is a map $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to A\times_W V$ with fixed endpoints; its two coordinate maps have exactly the fixed endpoints on the right and equal composites to $W$. Conversely those coordinate maps give the unique map into the pullback. These identifications commute with every simplicial operator.

source.place: Arrow mapping-space construction preceding Proposition 4.6.1.22; degreewise pullback calculation written out by the worker.

proof.text: The map $s:V\to W$ from step 1 is in particular an inner fibration. The last assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] therefore says that $U_V(a_V,b_V)\to U_W(a_W,b_W)$ is a Kan fibration between Kan complexes. All the other $U$ spaces here are Kan by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] to the identity in step 2: inserting the constant path gives a weak homotopy equivalence $$c_U:U_T(a,b)\longrightarrow P\bigl(U_A(a_A,b_A)\to U_W(a_W,b_W)\leftarrow U_V(a_V,b_V)\bigr).$$ Here $P$ denotes precisely the path-space pullback in that cited statement.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.7, using the arrow mapping-space Kan fibration of Proposition 4.6.1.22 (01P8).

proof.text: Let $M_Z=\operatorname{Map}_Z(a_Z,b_Z)$ for $Z=A,V,W$, and put $M_T=\operatorname{Map}_T(a,b)$. Restriction gives a constant-path comparison $c_M:M_T\to P(M_A\to M_W\leftarrow M_V)$. The natural right-pinch inclusions of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] give a strictly commuting square with top map $c_M$, bottom map $c_U$, left map $j_T$ and right map $P(j_A,j_W,j_V)$. Strict commutation follows because each pinch map is precomposition by the same simplicial map and sends constant paths to constant paths. The left map is a homotopy equivalence, and the right map is a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance]. Since the bottom map is a weak homotopy equivalence by step 3, the top map $c_M$ is one too: on components and every based homotopy group the equation $P(j_A,j_W,j_V)c_M=c_Uj_T$ expresses its induced map as a composite of isomorphisms after cancelling the right vertical isomorphism. This proves the comparison for every ordered pair $a,b$ of objects of $T$.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10, its natural pinch maps, and Proposition 3.4.0.9 (032B); agent-written comparison argument.

proof.text: Now take $\epsilon=\triangleright$ and $a=q(u)$, $b=q(t)$, for any $t\in X$. The comparison map defining the homotopy-pullback square in [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] is exactly the composite $$\operatorname{Map}_X(u,t)\xrightarrow{q_*}\operatorname{Map}_T(q(u),q(t))\xrightarrow{c_M}P\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_A(u|_K,t|_K)\to\operatorname{Map}_W(pu|_K,pt|_K)\leftarrow\operatorname{Map}_V(pu,pt)\bigr).$$ Both composites send a simplex to its restriction, its image under $p$, and the constant path at their equal further restrictions. The second arrow is a weak homotopy equivalence by step 4. Thus the composite is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if $q_*$ is: cancel the induced isomorphisms on components and all based homotopy groups. Quantifying over $t$, the left condition is precisely that $u$ is a $p$-colimit diagram, while the right condition is precisely that $u$ is $q$-initial by [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary].

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.19, condition (2), colimit dual; relative-initial predicate of Proposition 7.1.5.16 (02WR).

proof.text: For $\epsilon=\triangleleft$ and each $t\in X$, apply step 4 to the ordered pair $a=q(t)$, $b=q(u)$. The defining comparison for the $p$-limit square is $$\operatorname{Map}_X(t,u)\xrightarrow{q_*}\operatorname{Map}_T(q(t),q(u))\xrightarrow{c_M}P\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_A(t|_K,u|_K)\to\operatorname{Map}_W(pt|_K,pu|_K)\leftarrow\operatorname{Map}_V(pt,pu)\bigr).$$ An $n$-simplex $\sigma$ of $\operatorname{Map}_X(t,u)$ is sent by either map to $(\sigma|_K,p\sigma,\operatorname{const}_{p(\sigma|_K)})$: restriction and postcomposition commute strictly, so the two endpoints of the displayed constant path coincide. This proves equality of the maps in every degree and with all simplicial operators. Since $c_M$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, the square is a homotopy pullback if and only if $q_*$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. For every $t$, these are exactly the $p$-limit condition of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] and the $q$-final condition of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary]. No construction of a universal diagram, and hence no existence assumption on other limits or colimits, entered any step.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.19, condition (2), and Proposition 7.1.6.13 (02XB); relative-final mapping-space predicate.

proof_origin.place: Direct proof from condition (2), using the existing arrow/pinched mapping-space and path-pullback lemmas; the source of Proposition 7.1.6.13 uses a different slice/fiber proof. Online sources read; archival copies wanted.

The statement is unchanged: p is an isofibration of quasicategories, K is any small simplicial set, the corner maps are isofibrations, and u is a p-colimit (p-limit) diagram exactly when it is corner-initial (corner-final). The parent (parameter-cone-extension) supplies the isofibration hypothesis. Step 1: the injective inclusion K into its cone and the corner/restriction clauses of isofibration-exponentiation give the quasicategories and the inner fibration s:V->W. Step 2 (marked elementary): the arrow space of the pullback T is strictly the pullback of the arrow spaces of A, V over W, because pullbacks are formed degreewise. Step 3: U_V->U_W is a Kan fibration by the last clause of isofibration-exponentiation, and the U spaces are Kan by pinch-comparison, so pullback-path-comparison makes the constant-path map an equivalence. Step 4: the pinch maps commute strictly with both spans by naturality, homotopy-pullback-invariance applies, and 2-out-of-3 transfers the equivalence to the pinched mapping spaces. Steps 5 and 6: the composite equals the defining comparison of def-coef-infinity-relative-cone, in the same corner order as the path lemma; cancelling the equivalence gives the colimit case and, with pair (q(t),q(u)), the limit case. relative-initial-boundary is used only for its defining clause. Route: all statements used are in unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, and def-cbc counts as a notion, so no tool use is needed. No SGA source is used. Edge cases checked: K empty reduces to p-initial; p from N[1] to a point with the edge 0->1 fails on both sides; p = id passes on both sides. No duplicates among the four relative-cone nodes compared. No fixes were made.
